SMTO-SKL-0151 — That Slack reaction was already there

GUID: d9edd9d8-a5bb-56dd-89a0-5fdb138a6367
Slug: slack-reaction-present
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to add a reaction that's already on that Slack message from the Slack account SMTO uses. Nothing needed to change, so SMTO left the message as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the message in Slack and check that the reaction is showing. Slack reported that this reaction from SMTO's Slack account is already on the message.
  2. If you meant a different emoji or a different message, ask the Agent for that specific emoji on that specific message. This request was for an emoji that's already there, so nothing new was added.

What success looks like

  • The message in Slack shows the reaction once from SMTO's Slack account.

If it still fails

  • If the reaction isn't showing in Slack, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Slack connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned already_reacted for reactions.add; the service treats the desired reaction as present and returns present=true, changed=false without another write.

What this means

  • Slack returns already_reacted for the selected principal, message and reaction. The provider reports the desired reaction already present, and the reaction service treats that as changed=false rather than issuing another write.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns already_reacted for the selected principal, message and reaction.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm the exact reaction request identity and provider result.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is needed: SlackService.reaction maps slack.reaction_present to a successful no-op (present=true, changed=false). If a different message or emoji was intended, issue add_reaction with the exact channel_id, ts and name.

Retry and execution caution

  • The desired reaction is already present; no additional write is needed.

How to verify the fix

  • The service returns present=true with changed=false.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The provider reports the desired reaction already present, and the reaction service treats that as changed=false rather than issuing another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
